description:
FILED s458ak, which did phase 4's RUNTIME half (accessor dispatch, #815, #811, #841) and MEASURED the two remaining emission arms rather than guessing at them.  BOTH numbers changed the picture, so read them before scheduling:

ARM A -- foreach-LIST read-only loop var (design SS4.4 "proven arm"; #810 rides it).  A read-only `for my $x (@a)` PROMOTES every element of @a to a box, once, and the array then pays box indirection on every later read FOREVER (promotion is monotone by design).  MEASURED: `my @a=(1..1000); for (1..30000) { for my $x (@a) { $s += $x } }` runs the loop in ~0.48 s where the never-promoting index spelling `for my $i (0..999) { $s += $a[$i] }` runs it in ~0.29 s (perl: 0.616 s and 0.708 s).  So the arm is worth ~40 % of a read-only foreach, and it would take that shape from 0.78x perl to ~0.47x.  REAL, and it is the one that also closes #810 honestly (a foreach alias to a LITERAL list is read-only in perl and writable in PCL).  COST: it is VarAnnotator verdict work -- the WHAT-TO-RUN table's name-resolution row, so the full sweep IS the gate, plus a gate-SET scan over both populations, a generation bump and the three artifacts.  Its own session.

ARM B -- the slice COPY position (the `slices` bench row).  DE-PRIORITISED BY MEASUREMENT: after s458ak's accessor work the `slices` row is 5.23x -> 3.21x and sb-sprof no longer shows make-p-box or the promotion arm anywhere in its top 19; what is left is the equal-hash lookups (21 %), p-array-fill's own construction and the key stringify.  The s457ai reading that "a slice in a COPY position still promotes" is TRUE but the bench never measured the ALLOCATION -- promotion is monotone, so 200k iterations over the same 50 slots promote once and then re-read boxes.  The prize is therefore the box INDIRECTION on the re-reads, which is the same prize as ARM A and is better bought there.  Do ARM A first and RE-MEASURE `slices` before spending anything on ARM B.

BAR for either arm: corpus-diff with every diff explained and probed vs perl, PCL_OPT=none equivalence, the elem-alias-01.t battery green under BOTH PCL_RAW_ELEMS settings, full sweep, companion op/ leg, generation bump + tools/rebuild-pack.
ARM A SHIPPED s459am; ARM B MEASURED AND RECOMMENDED FOR CLOSURE (task #882).

ARM A, as designed: a NEW verdict key `foreach_ro` in VarAnnotator (Kind-A
gate `foreach-raw`), consumed by Parser2's foreach lowering, which emits
`p-foreach-raw` â a thin twin of `p-foreach` over a shared `%expand-foreach`
expander, differing ONLY in the element accessor.  `%p-foreach-elt-raw` binds
the slot AS IT STANDS: a raw value directly, an existing BOX unchanged (so a
reference keeps its is-ref, and tie/magic/blessed cells keep their dispatch â
unboxing here would hand the loop variable the referent), a hole as undef.
No promotion, no allocation.
DELIBERATELY NOT `unboxable`: the loop variable's storage verdict is
unchanged, so every other consumer sees exactly what it saw and the BODY's
emission is byte-identical.  The only emission change anywhere is the macro
name â proved over the 111-file corpus (14 files differ, every diff line is
the rename plus two pretty-printer re-flows caused by the 4-char-longer
symbol) and over all 22 lib shims (emission-ab DIFF 5 / RCDIFF 0; after the
tool's own path+gen normalization the residue is empty).

THE ONE REAL TRAP, found by the probe battery BEFORE it shipped, and now the
reason Pl/t/foreach-raw-01.t exists: THE ANNOTATOR'S REASON LIST IS NOT THE
WHOLE WRITE STORY.  A statement-root `$v = RHS`, a root coercing compound
`$v *= 2` and a root `$v++` are deliberately NOT boxing events (a raw slot
stores them fine), so they leave NO reason and are recorded as write FACTS
(write_fam / incdec_root / init_bad / write_obj).  For a foreach ALIAS every
one of them is a write that must reach the container.  A first version keyed
only on "reasons == exactly [foreach-alias]" fired on
`for my $o (@a) { for my $i (@$o) { $i *= 2 } }`, `(p-*= $i 2)` box-set a raw
value, and the doubling vanished SILENTLY.  The licence now tests the facts
too.  DO NOT re-derive this: a future widening of the arm must ask the same
question of any new native-write shape.

MEASURED (tools/bench-exec.pl, new `feread` row = this task's own program):
0.71x perl -> 0.47x, PCL 0.3970 s -> 0.2746 s (-31 %), A/B through the arm's
own gate in one session.  `slices` 3.02x -> 3.06x, i.e. unmoved â see #882.

BAR MET: corpus-diff 14 files, every diff explained (rename only); emission-ab
over lib 22 files, rename only, RCDIFF 0; gate PASS 191/6416; full sweep GATE
clean TOTAL 18340 (+0), drops 5 = census, pack.t 5636/89 = baseline; gate-SET
scan 638 x 2 populations IDENTICAL; Pl/t/elem-alias-01.t + foreach-raw-01.t +
passes-01.t green under BOTH PCL_RAW_ELEMS settings; PCL_OPT=none equivalence
in passes-01.t (shape rows AND the run-output row); generation v2-500 with all
three artifacts regenerated; guard Pl/t/foreach-raw-01.t (28 rows) inverse-
verified on an e9296cb worktree (exactly the 4 shape rows fail there, all 24
behaviour/refusal rows pass â they are perl-correct on both trees, which is
the point).

THREE Pl/t SHAPE ROWS WERE STALE against this change and were repaired in the
same commit (the s416 standing rule): statements-01.t "foreach with variable",
parser2-01.t "reverse 1..3 is NOT split", parser2-02.t "foreach continue".
Each asserts membership of the foreach FAMILY, not which arm binds the loop
variable, and each widened to `p-foreach(?:-raw)?` â the convention those very
files already use for `p-foreach-range(?:-raw)?`.  The specific new fact they
stop pinning is pinned instead, in the same commit, by foreach-raw-01.t's 4
fire rows and 9 refusal rows.

#810 (a foreach alias to a LITERAL list is read-only in perl and writable in
PCL): the READ-ONLY half is now honest â `for my $x (1,2,3)` binds raw values
and allocates nothing (guard row in foreach-raw-01.t).  The WRITING half is
untouched and still diverges: perl dies "Modification of a read-only value",
PCL substitutes.  #810 stays OPEN for that half.

STILL NOT DONE from this task: E2c' (the writes_args-gated raw pass into @_).

======================================================================
E2c' MEASURED AND NOT SHIPPED (s460ao, agent AO, round 17) — with a
DESIGN ASK for Fable, because the measurement changed the question.
======================================================================

STRUCTURAL FINDING FIRST, because it makes E2c' much smaller than the design
sketch implies: `p-flatten-args` is called in the CALLEE, not at the call site
(`(let ((@_ (p-flatten-args %_args))) ...)`, Parser2.pm:10474/10534).  So
E2c's "the callee is KNOWN and its writes_args fact is false" is not a
call-site lookup at all — it is a fact about the sub BEING LOWERED, available
right there from `_sub_writes_args($sub)`.  The change is ~5 lines of emission
plus one optional runtime argument.  Whoever schedules this should not go
looking for the call-site plumbing the design describes.

THE OWED POPULATION MEASUREMENT (design doc §5 lists it; taken here):

    corpus            named subs   writes_args FALSE      call sites   passing a whole @array
    perl-tests (111)     759        695  (91.6 %)            9885        741  (7.5 %)
    lib shims   (20)     299        237  (79.3 %)             205         12  (5.9 %)

So ~9 in 10 subs are ELIGIBLE, but only ~1 call site in 14 ever reaches the
promoting arm at all — and promotion is monotone, so for those the saving is
one allocation per element ONCE, plus keeping the array raw for its LATER
reads.  That second half is the whole prize, and #883 now bounds it: the
raw-vs-boxed read difference is 31 % of the read portion of a loop (measured
both ways with PCL_RAW_ELEMS), which on the one benched flatten shape is ~15 %
of the row.  No bench row exercises E2c's own shape.

THE DESIGN ASK (this is why it was not just shipped):

E2c' INVERTS THE SAFETY POLARITY OF AN EXISTING FACT, for arrays.  Today a
whole-array argument is promoted UNCONDITIONALLY, so `f(@a)` followed by
`$_[0] = 1` writes through even if `writes_args` is wrong about f.  E2c'
removes that net: a false negative becomes a SILENT failure to write through —
the design's own "one unaffordable failure mode" (§4.3 option (b), "rejected
outright"), now merely gated on a fact.  In mitigation, the fact is ALREADY
trusted permissively elsewhere: #189 turns writes_args TRUE into an
`arg-to-writer` boxing event at call sites, so a wrong FALSE already loses a
write-through for SCALAR arguments.  E2c' therefore adds no new KIND of trust
— but it does widen the blast radius from scalars to whole arrays, and it does
so for a measured ~15 %-of-one-shape prize with no benched consumer.

RECOMMENDATION: ship it only with (a) a Fable ruling that widening
writes_args' permissive use to arrays is acceptable, and (b) a bench row that
actually exercises the shape, so the win is a number rather than an
expectation.  It is cheap to build once ruled; it is not cheap to debug if the
fact is ever wrong.  Nothing about it blocks the rest of phase 4.
  RULED s460f (Fable, 2026-09-01): E2c' is NOT SHIPPED and #862 CLOSES.  s460ao's structural finding stands (p-flatten-args runs in the CALLEE, so the fact is _sub_writes_args there, no call-site plumbing) but the change INVERTS writes_args' safety polarity for arrays: today a wrong FALSE still writes through (unconditional promotion), under E2c' it becomes a SILENT LOST WRITE -- the codebase's worst failure mode -- for a prize no bench measures.  Re-open ONLY with (a) a measured prize on a real row AND (b) a verification story for the polarity (a die-on-mismatch checked mode, or a writes_args audit gate).  ARM A shipped s459am; ARM B closed by measurement (#882); #883 measured 15% of one row and declined s460ao.
subject: boxed aggregates PHASE 4, the EMISSION half -- ARM A SHIPPED s459am; ARM B closed (#882); E2c' MEASURED s460ao and NOT shipped (population + prize bounded; carries a Fable design ask on widening writes_args' permissive use to arrays)
